senses.definition_en: politicianese, political jargon, language used by politicians

examples.english: "Politicianese" is the cultist jargon of politicians, and sometimes also of the best situated professionals, the leaders of economic and administrative life.
examples.ref: 2009 March 13, Amando de Miguel, “Apuntes sobre el politiqués”, in Libertad Digital:
examples.text: El "politiqués" es la jerga cultista de los políticos, a veces también de los profesionales mejor situados, los dirigentes de la vida económica y administrativa.
examples.translation: "Politicianese" is the cultist jargon of politicians, and sometimes also of the best situated professionals, the leaders of economic and administrative life.

examples.english: They speak but are not understood; they talk but are not comprehended. What has caused us to slide to this delusional point? We study 'politicianese'
examples.ref: 2020 March 2, Sergio Soto, “Radiografía del 'politiqués' o ese lenguaje que hablan los políticos”, in Cadena SER:
examples.text: Hablan pero no se les entiende; dicen pero no se les comprende ¿Qué nos ha traído hasta este delirante punto en que las cosas se deslizan? Estudiamos el 'politiqués'
examples.translation: They speak but are not understood; they talk but are not comprehended. What has caused us to slide to this delusional point? We study 'politicianese'

examples.english: The new meanings of politicianese, the jargon that politicians apparently need to use to distinguish themselves from those who vote for them.
examples.ref: 2015 August 1, Fernanda Tabarés, “Una de politiqués”, in La Voz de Galicia:
examples.text: Nuevas acepciones de politiqués, la jerga que al parecer necesitan los políticos para distinguirse de quienes los votan.
examples.translation: The new meanings of politicianese, the jargon that politicians apparently need to use to distinguish themselves from those who vote for them.

examples.english: In this sense, one of the most accurate and hilarious contributions on the subject, the work of the sociologist Amando de Miguel, is the allusion to politicianese as a sort of pseudo-language full of rhetoric, petulance and an overdose of clichés that, when taken to the extreme, derive into a Tertullian dialect that even its own users do not understand after putting down their microphones.
examples.ref: 2019 November 8, Myriam Z. Alvéniz, “El politiqués o la esterilidad de un idioma”, in La Provincia:
examples.text: En este sentido, una de las aportaciones más certeras e hilarantes sobre el tema, obra del sociólogo Amando de Miguel, es la alusión al politiqués como pseudoidioma pleno de retórica, petulancia y sobredosis de latiguillos insoportables que, llevados al extremo, derivan en el dialecto tertulianés y que ni sus propios usuarios entienden a micrófono cerrado.
examples.translation: In this sense, one of the most accurate and hilarious contributions on the subject, the work of the sociologist Amando de Miguel, is the allusion to politicianese as a sort of pseudo-language full of rhetoric, petulance and an overdose of clichés that, when taken to the extreme, derive into a Tertullian dialect that even its own users do not understand after putting down their microphones.

glosses: politicianese, political jargon, language used by politicians
